scale.statement: The characteristic length at this slot is the critical Turing wavelength λ_c = 319.2 µm.

evolutionary_history.what_changes: Nothing in λ_c changes across a chronospecies boundary, because this series has no predecessor and no successor. Relative to a smaller embryonic field of the same Holocene species, the number of selected periods N = round(L / 319.2 µm) changes: a field with L < 319.2 µm supports no ocellus, and the six-wavelength dorsal patch used here (1915.2 µm) supports six. That geometric cutoff is developmental, not a fossil-species parameter copied from another slot.

equations.kinetics: ∂u/∂t = Du ∇²u + γ (a − u + u²v),  ∂v/∂t = Dv ∇²v + γ (b − u²v)
equations.onset_wavenumber: k_c² = (Dv fu + Du gv) / (2 Du Dv)
equations.turing_margin: R = h² / (4 Du Dv det J) with h = Dv fu + Du gv; onset iff h > 0 and R > 1
equations.amplitude: Stuart–Landau growth of the critical radial mode, α(t) from 0 to the saturated ocellus

parameters.note: γ is not free: it is solved so the onset wavelength is exactly 319.2 µm. Equal diffusion Dv = Du is the ablation (R = 0).

boundary_conditions: Periodic boundaries on the numerical Schnakenberg check (pass 2). The rendered ocellus is the isotropic critical-circle mode (a radial target) on the gallery plate, with a fixed footer outside the fitness crop.
state_variables: α Stuart–Landau amplitude of the ocellus
empirical_claims: Turing (1952) showed a homogeneous reaction–diffusion state can be unstable at a finite wavenumber k_c.
Prum & Williamson (2002) showed reaction–diffusion on a growing feather germ reproduces within-feather bars, spots, and ocelli.
Harris et al. (2005) gave molecular evidence that an Shh/Bmp2 activator–inhibitor interaction patterns barb ridges in embryonic Gallus gallus.
This slot assigns the Holocene primordium-scale wavelength λ_c = 319.2 µm. The gallery plate's painted 100 µm bar is a different, inconsistent ruler and is reported separately.

ocellus_plate.role: Canonical plate for image-fitness and radial-profile goodness-of-fit.
